# C1. Site overview

```{python}
import json
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import display


def find_project_root():
    for candidate in (Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents):
        if (candidate / "data" / "raw").is_dir() and (
            candidate / "flux4student" / "sites.json"
        ).is_file():
            return candidate
    raise FileNotFoundError(
        "Could not locate the project root containing data/raw and flux4student/sites.json."
    )


project_root = find_project_root()
raw_dir = project_root / "data" / "raw"
zip_files = sorted(raw_dir.glob("*_FLUXNET_*.zip"))
if len(zip_files) != 5:
    raise ValueError(f"Expected five FLUXNET zip files in {raw_dir}; found {len(zip_files)}.")

keep = [
    "TIMESTAMP_START", "TIMESTAMP_END", "TA_F", "SW_IN_F", "VPD_F", "P_F",
    "NETRAD", "G_F_MDS", "H_F_MDS", "H_F_MDS_QC", "LE_F_MDS", "LE_F_MDS_QC",
    "NEE_VUT_REF", "NEE_VUT_REF_QC", "GPP_NT_VUT_REF", "RECO_NT_VUT_REF",
]


def read_hh(zip_file):
    zip_file = Path(zip_file)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_file) as archive:
        members = [name for name in archive.namelist() if "FLUXMET_HH" in name]
        if not members:
            raise ValueError(f"No FLUXMET_HH file found in {zip_file.name}.")
        with archive.open(members[0]) as csv_file:
            hh = pd.read_csv(
                csv_file,
                na_values=[-9999],
                usecols=lambda column: column in keep,
                dtype={"TIMESTAMP_START": str, "TIMESTAMP_END": str},
            )

    hh["time"] = pd.to_datetime(hh["TIMESTAMP_START"], format="%Y%m%d%H%M")
    hh["site"] = zip_file.stem.split("_", maxsplit=2)[1]
    return hh


hh_all = pd.concat([read_hh(zip_file) for zip_file in zip_files], ignore_index=True)
sites = sorted(hh_all["site"].unique())
if len(sites) != 5:
    raise ValueError(f"Expected five distinct tower sites; found {sites}.")

registry = json.loads(
    (project_root / "flux4student" / "sites.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
)
registry_by_site = {row["id"]: row for row in registry}
missing_metadata = sorted(set(sites) - set(registry_by_site))
if missing_metadata:
    raise ValueError(f"Missing site metadata for: {', '.join(missing_metadata)}.")

country_names = {
    "AU": "Australia",
    "CN": "China",
    "CZ": "Czech Republic",
    "IT": "Italy",
    "US": "United States",
}
meta = pd.DataFrame(
    [
        {
            "SITE_ID": site,
            "SITE_NAME": registry_by_site[site]["name"],
            "COUNTRY": country_names.get(site[:2], site[:2]),
            "IGBP": registry_by_site[site]["igbp"],
            "LAT": registry_by_site[site]["lat"],
            "LON": registry_by_site[site]["lon"],
            "FIRST_YEAR": registry_by_site[site]["first"],
            "LAST_YEAR": registry_by_site[site]["last"],
            "HUB": registry_by_site[site]["hub"],
            "CITATION": registry_by_site[site]["cite"],
        }
        for site in sites
    ]
)

display(meta)
```

The site information comes from the tracked `flux4student/sites.json` registry,
so the report does not depend on a separate `data/site_snapshot.csv` file.

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
ax.scatter(meta["LON"], meta["LAT"])

for _, row in meta.iterrows():
    ax.text(row["LON"], row["LAT"], row["SITE_ID"], fontsize=9)

ax.set_xlabel("Longitude (degrees)")
ax.set_ylabel("Latitude (degrees)")
ax.set_title("Locations of the five flux towers")
ax.set_xlim(-180, 180)
ax.set_ylim(-60, 85)
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

# C2. Data coverage

Measured coverage is the share of half-hours where `NEE_VUT_REF_QC` equals zero.

```{python}
hh_all["year"] = hh_all["time"].dt.year
coverage = (
    hh_all.assign(measured=hh_all["NEE_VUT_REF_QC"].eq(0))
    .groupby(["site", "year"])["measured"]
    .mean()
    .unstack("year")
    .reindex(sites)
)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 4))
image = ax.imshow(
    coverage.to_numpy(),
    aspect="auto",
    interpolation="nearest",
    vmin=0,
    vmax=1,
    cmap="viridis",
)
ax.set_yticks(np.arange(len(coverage.index)), labels=coverage.index)
ax.set_xticks(
    np.arange(len(coverage.columns)),
    labels=coverage.columns.astype(int),
    rotation=45,
)
ax.set_xlabel("Year")
ax.set_ylabel("Site")
ax.set_title("Share of half-hours with measured NEE (QC = 0)")
colorbar = fig.colorbar(image, ax=ax)
colorbar.set_label("Measured share")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()

mean_coverage = coverage.mean(axis=1).sort_values(ascending=False)
best_site = mean_coverage.index[0]
best_years = coverage.loc[best_site].dropna().sort_values(ascending=False).head(3)
year_summary = ", ".join(
    f"{int(year)} ({share:.1%})" for year, share in best_years.items()
)
print(
    f"{best_site} has the highest average measured share across its years "
    f"({mean_coverage.iloc[0]:.1%}); its three best years are {year_summary}."
)
```

# C3. Summary statistics

The statistics below use half-hourly values, except for `P_F`: precipitation is
summed by calendar year, then its mean, minimum and maximum annual totals are
reported. Missingness is the share of half-hours without a value. Units are
included in each variable label.

```{python}
variable_units = {
    "TA_F": "deg C",
    "SW_IN_F": "W m-2",
    "VPD_F": "hPa",
    "P_F": "mm/year (annual sums)",
    "NEE_VUT_REF": "umol CO2 m-2 s-1",
    "GPP_NT_VUT_REF": "umol CO2 m-2 s-1",
    "RECO_NT_VUT_REF": "umol CO2 m-2 s-1",
    "H_F_MDS": "W m-2",
    "LE_F_MDS": "W m-2",
}

for variable, unit in variable_units.items():
    rows = []
    for site, group in hh_all.groupby("site", sort=True):
        values = group[variable]
        if variable == "P_F":
            annual_values = (
                pd.DataFrame({"year": group["time"].dt.year, "value": values})
                .groupby("year")["value"]
                .sum(min_count=1)
            )
            mean_value = annual_values.mean()
            min_value = annual_values.min()
            max_value = annual_values.max()
            statistic = f"annual total ({unit})"
        else:
            mean_value = values.mean()
            min_value = values.min()
            max_value = values.max()
            statistic = f"value ({unit})"

        rows.append(
            {
                "Site": site,
                f"Mean {statistic}": mean_value,
                f"Minimum {statistic}": min_value,
                f"Maximum {statistic}": max_value,
                "Missing (%)": values.isna().mean() * 100,
            }
        )

    print(variable)
    display(pd.DataFrame(rows).round(2))
```

# C4. Daily time series

Daily values are the arithmetic means of the half-hourly fluxes. The conversion
is `1 umol CO2 m-2 s-1 = 1.0378 g C m-2 d-1`; negative NEE values are retained.

```{python}
carbon_fluxes = ["NEE_VUT_REF", "GPP_NT_VUT_REF", "RECO_NT_VUT_REF"]
daily = (
    hh_all.set_index("time")
    .groupby("site")[carbon_fluxes]
    .resample("D")
    .mean()
    .reset_index()
)
daily_gC = daily.copy()
daily_gC[carbon_fluxes] = daily_gC[carbon_fluxes] * 1.0378

fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(sites), 1, figsize=(13, 2.8 * len(sites)), sharex=True)
for ax, site in zip(axes, sites):
    site_daily = daily_gC.loc[daily_gC["site"] == site]
    for variable, label in [
        ("NEE_VUT_REF", "NEE"),
        ("GPP_NT_VUT_REF", "GPP"),
        ("RECO_NT_VUT_REF", "RECO"),
    ]:
        ax.plot(site_daily["time"], site_daily[variable], linewidth=0.55, label=label)
    ax.axhline(0, color="0.5", linewidth=0.6)
    ax.set_ylabel("g C m-2 d-1")
    ax.set_title(site, loc="left")
    ax.legend(ncol=3, fontsize=8)

axes[-1].set_xlabel("Date (local standard time)")
fig.suptitle("Daily NEE, GPP and RECO", y=1.002)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The half-hourly daily NEE mean is compared with the daily `FLUXMET_DD` NEE
product for one site as an aggregation check.

```{python}
check_site = sites[0]
check_zip = next(
    path for path in zip_files
    if path.stem.split("_", maxsplit=2)[1] == check_site
)
with zipfile.ZipFile(check_zip) as archive:
    daily_members = [name for name in archive.namelist() if "FLUXMET_DD" in name]
    if not daily_members:
        raise ValueError(f"No FLUXMET_DD file found in {check_zip.name}.")
    with archive.open(daily_members[0]) as csv_file:
        daily_product = pd.read_csv(
            csv_file,
            usecols=lambda column: column in {"TIMESTAMP", "NEE_VUT_REF"},
            dtype={"TIMESTAMP": str},
            na_values=[-9999],
        )

if "TIMESTAMP" not in daily_product or "NEE_VUT_REF" not in daily_product:
    raise ValueError("The daily product must contain TIMESTAMP and NEE_VUT_REF columns.")

daily_product["date"] = pd.to_datetime(
    daily_product["TIMESTAMP"], format="%Y%m%d", errors="coerce"
)
daily_product = daily_product.set_index("date")["NEE_VUT_REF"].rename("FLUXMET_DD")
half_hourly_daily = (
    hh_all.loc[hh_all["site"] == check_site]
    .assign(date=lambda frame: frame["time"].dt.normalize())
    .groupby("date")["NEE_VUT_REF"]
    .mean()
    .rename("Half-hourly daily mean")
)
daily_comparison = pd.concat([half_hourly_daily, daily_product], axis=1).dropna()
if daily_comparison.empty:
    raise ValueError("No matching dates found for the daily aggregation check.")

mae = (
    daily_comparison["Half-hourly daily mean"] - daily_comparison["FLUXMET_DD"]
).abs().mean()
print(
    f"{check_site}: compared {len(daily_comparison):,} days; "
    f"mean absolute difference = {mae:.3f} umol CO2 m-2 s-1."
)
```

# C5. Diurnal cycles

Seasons are assigned from each site's latitude. Northern-hemisphere seasons are
DJF (winter), MAM (spring), JJA (summer) and SON (autumn); the season mapping is
reversed for southern-hemisphere sites. Time of day is local standard time.

```{python}
north_season = {
    12: "Winter", 1: "Winter", 2: "Winter",
    3: "Spring", 4: "Spring", 5: "Spring",
    6: "Summer", 7: "Summer", 8: "Summer",
    9: "Autumn", 10: "Autumn", 11: "Autumn",
}
south_season = {
    6: "Winter", 7: "Winter", 8: "Winter",
    9: "Spring", 10: "Spring", 11: "Spring",
    12: "Summer", 1: "Summer", 2: "Summer",
    3: "Autumn", 4: "Autumn", 5: "Autumn",
}
season_colors = {
    "Winter": "tab:blue",
    "Spring": "tab:green",
    "Summer": "tab:red",
    "Autumn": "tab:orange",
}
latitude_by_site = meta.set_index("SITE_ID")["LAT"]
diurnal_parts = []

for site, group in hh_all.groupby("site", sort=True):
    part = group[["time", "NEE_VUT_REF", "LE_F_MDS"]].copy()
    season_lookup = north_season if latitude_by_site[site] >= 0 else south_season
    part["season"] = part["time"].dt.month.map(season_lookup)
    part["hour"] = part["time"].dt.hour + part["time"].dt.minute / 60
    part["site"] = site
    diurnal_parts.append(part)

diurnal = pd.concat(diurnal_parts, ignore_index=True)
diurnal_means = (
    diurnal.groupby(["site", "season", "hour"])[["NEE_VUT_REF", "LE_F_MDS"]]
    .mean()
    .reset_index()
)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(sites), 2, figsize=(12, 3 * len(sites)), sharex=True)
for row, site in enumerate(sites):
    site_means = diurnal_means.loc[diurnal_means["site"] == site]
    for column, (variable, ylabel) in enumerate(
        [
            ("NEE_VUT_REF", "NEE (umol CO2 m-2 s-1)"),
            ("LE_F_MDS", "LE (W m-2)"),
        ]
    ):
        ax = axes[row, column]
        for season in ["Winter", "Spring", "Summer", "Autumn"]:
            curve = site_means.loc[site_means["season"] == season]
            if not curve.empty:
                ax.plot(
                    curve["hour"],
                    curve[variable],
                    color=season_colors[season],
                    label=season,
                )
        ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
        ax.set_title(f"{site}: {variable}", loc="left")
        ax.set_xticks(np.arange(0, 24, 4))
        if row == 0:
            ax.legend(ncol=4, fontsize=8)

axes[-1, 0].set_xlabel("Hour of day (local standard time)")
axes[-1, 1].set_xlabel("Hour of day (local standard time)")
fig.suptitle("Seasonal mean diurnal cycles", y=1.002)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

# C6. Your reading

## Energy balance

The tower with the most valid observations is selected. Only half-hours with
measured sensible and latent heat (`H_F_MDS_QC == 0` and `LE_F_MDS_QC == 0`)
and non-missing values for all four plotted fluxes are used.

```{python}
energy_counts = {}
for site, group in hh_all.groupby("site"):
    measured = (
        group["H_F_MDS_QC"].eq(0)
        & group["LE_F_MDS_QC"].eq(0)
        & group[["H_F_MDS", "LE_F_MDS", "NETRAD", "G_F_MDS"]].notna().all(axis=1)
    )
    energy_counts[site] = int(measured.sum())

energy_site = max(energy_counts, key=energy_counts.get)
if energy_counts[energy_site] < 2:
    raise ValueError("No site has enough measured half-hours for an energy-balance fit.")

energy_data = hh_all.loc[hh_all["site"] == energy_site]
measured = (
    energy_data["H_F_MDS_QC"].eq(0)
    & energy_data["LE_F_MDS_QC"].eq(0)
    & energy_data[["H_F_MDS", "LE_F_MDS", "NETRAD", "G_F_MDS"]].notna().all(axis=1)
)
energy_data = energy_data.loc[measured]
x = (energy_data["NETRAD"] - energy_data["G_F_MDS"]).to_numpy()
y = (energy_data["H_F_MDS"] + energy_data["LE_F_MDS"]).to_numpy()
slope, intercept = np.polyfit(x, y, 1)

plot_indices = np.linspace(0, len(x) - 1, min(len(x), 20000), dtype=int)
line_min = min(float(x.min()), float(y.min()))
line_max = max(float(x.max()), float(y.max()))
line = np.linspace(line_min, line_max, 100)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 6))
ax.scatter(x[plot_indices], y[plot_indices], s=5, alpha=0.18, rasterized=True)
ax.plot(line, line, color="black", linestyle="--", label="1:1 line")
ax.plot(
    line,
    slope * line + intercept,
    color="crimson",
    label=f"Linear fit (slope = {slope:.2f})",
)
ax.set_xlabel("NETRAD - G_F_MDS (W m-2)")
ax.set_ylabel("H_F_MDS + LE_F_MDS (W m-2)")
ax.set_title(f"Energy balance: {energy_site} (n = {len(x):,})")
ax.legend()
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
print(f"Linear-fit slope for {energy_site}: {slope:.3f}.")
```

## Data and citation

The site product citations are taken from the most recent FLUXNET Shuttle
snapshot in `data/snapshots` when available. If a snapshot is not present, the
report uses `data/raw/CITATIONS.txt`, then the tracked site registry.

```{python}
from IPython.display import Markdown

snapshot_files = sorted(
    (project_root / "data" / "snapshots").glob("fluxnet_shuttle_snapshot_*.csv"),
    reverse=True,
)
citation_by_site = {}
citation_source = None

if snapshot_files:
    snapshot = pd.read_csv(snapshot_files[0], dtype={"site_id": str})
    required_columns = {"site_id", "product_citation"}
    if not required_columns.issubset(snapshot.columns):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{snapshot_files[0].name} must contain site_id and product_citation columns."
        )
    citation_by_site = (
        snapshot.dropna(subset=["product_citation"])
        .set_index("site_id")["product_citation"]
        .to_dict()
    )
    citation_source = snapshot_files[0].name

if not all(site in citation_by_site for site in sites):
    citation_file = raw_dir / "CITATIONS.txt"
    if citation_file.is_file():
        for line in citation_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            if ": " in line:
                site, citation = line.split(": ", maxsplit=1)
                if site in sites and citation.strip():
                    citation_by_site.setdefault(site, citation.strip())

for site in sites:
    citation_by_site.setdefault(site, registry_by_site[site]["cite"])

display(
    Markdown(
        f"Site product citations (snapshot: `{citation_source}`):\n\n"
        + "\n".join(
            f"- **{site}**: {citation_by_site[site]}" for site in sites
        )
    )
)
```

Pastorello et al. (2020). The FLUXNET2015 dataset and the ONEFlux processing
pipeline for eddy covariance data. *Scientific Data* 7, 225.
[https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0534-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0534-3)

> FLUXNET data products were produced and harmonized by eddy covariance regional
> networks and data processing centers, including AmeriFlux, ChinaFlux, European
> Fluxes Database, ICOS, JapanFlux, KoFlux, OzFlux, SAEON, and TERN. These products
> also include a modified version of ERA5 hourly data provided by the Copernicus
> Climate Change Service.
